notes.text: Fix for the 'SupportsRecursion' issue: added a third link, https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.readerwriterlockslim.enterwritelock. From memory, its Exceptions section lists LockRecursionException for 'the current thread has entered read mode and doesn't already own a write lock, so trying to enter the lock in write mode would create the possibility of a deadlock'. This case is listed separately from the NoRecursion case, so it applies under either policy. No excerpt of that page was provided, so the fact-checker should confirm the wording. Partial evidence in the provided EnterUpgradeableReadLock excerpt: it lists, separately from the NoRecursion case, 'The current thread has entered read mode, so trying to enter upgradeable mode would create the possibility of a deadlock'.

Claim 'only one thread at a time can be in upgradeable mode, ordinary readers are not blocked' is kept. I hold it with high but not full certainty: the class remarks and the EnterUpgradeableReadLock remarks state that only one thread can be in upgradeable mode at any time. The provided excerpts are truncated before that remark. The EnterUpgradeableReadLock excerpt does confirm 'Upgradeable mode allows the thread to upgrade the read lock as needed, without risk of deadlocks'. Please verify against the full remarks.

Fixed an overstatement in the explanation. NoRecursion no longer reads as forbidding entry 'in any mode': the text now says that the upgradeable-to-write transition is allowed. The sandbox-verified fixedSource relies on that transition and prints 10\n10.
Hint softened in both locales, as the verifier suggested. It no longer names the read-to-write transition.
bugLineSets kept as [[12, 19], [12], [19]]. Line 12 is the root cause and line 19 is the throwing call. The answer now says explicitly in both locales that line 12, line 19 or both are accepted.
